text:
Nina: Heads-up — customer acme-platform says their reserved GPU hours tanked last night but token burn stayed tiny (~14k). They flagged an unexpected 62h consumption on pool rp-acme-platform-01.
Maya: which pool id and invoice line?
Nina: rp-acme-platform-01. Invoice shows `Reserved GPU hours: 62h (2026-12-15)`. Their dashboard graph shows steady ~24h actual serving time + small bursts.
Eli: low tokens + high GPU hours typically points to warmup/idle nodes being counted. Did they run any deploys or healthchecks?
Nina: customer timeline: multiple small canary restarts from 02:04–02:25 UTC. They say the canary should not bill warmup <5m.
deploy-bot: autoscaler: scaled up 3 warmup nodes for pool rp-acme-platform-01 at 2026-12-15T02:04:12Z; scaled down at 2026-12-15T02:08:50Z; repeated at 02:12 and 02:18.
Sam: pulling metering rows for that window now. Query: ```GET /internal/metering?pool=rp-acme-platform-01&from=2026-12-15T00:00:00Z&to=2026-12-16T00:00:00Z```
Sam: sample metering lines: ```
1964257452, rp-acme-platform-01, instance-start, billed_gpu_hours: 2.5
1964257510, rp-acme-platform-01, instance-warmup, billed_gpu_hours: 2.8
1964257650, rp-acme-platform-01, instance-init, billed_gpu_hours: 1.7
```
Zane: that suggests warmup/init phases were attributed to billable reserved hours. We recently rolled a change to exclude warmup <5m via feature flag `metering.exclude_short_warmup`. Could be a flag flip.
Maya: Policy note: reserved pools should not bill transient warmups shorter than 5 minutes. The 2026-12-01 rollout added the exclusion but left a tag-lookup step that can override per-pool flags.
Eli: I inspected the pool metadata: rp-acme-platform-01 has tag `canary:true` but the deploy pipeline emitted `canary=yes` (string mismatch), so the flag lookup returned null and defaulted to false.
Sam: I can reproduce locally: create pool, toggle tag to `canary=yes`, run canary deploy -> metering shows warmup billed. Repro commands: ```
redwoodctl pool create --id rp-test-warmup --commit 720 --region us-west1
redwoodctl tags set rp-test-warmup canary=yes
redwoodctl deploy --pool rp-test-warmup --canary true --image model:v2-canary
curl "https://internal.api/metering?pool=rp-test-warmup&from=$(date -u -Iseconds -d '-1 hour')&to=$(date -u -Iseconds)"
```
Nina: customer is asking for immediate credit and a short explanation.
Sam: quick reconciliation: billed reserved hours 62h, dashboard-serving estimate 24h. Delta = 38h. Warmup event aggregation explains ~34h across repeated canary restarts.
Zane: root cause: deploy tag normalization bug -> flag effectively disabled -> short warmups billed. Plan: patch deploy pipeline tag normalization to accept yes/true/1, add unit test, and backfill a server-side safety check for the feature flag lookup. I'll open PR `fix/normalize-canary-tag` and push hotfix to canaries. ETA 90m.
Maya: action items:
- Sam: export full metering CSV + event log for 2026-12-15 window and attach to ticket (ETA 30m).
- Zane: push hotfix and schedule rollout to prod canaries (ETA 90m).
- Eli: draft customer credit message and propose provisional credit of 38 GPU-hours + a goodwill SLA day (ETA 60m).
- Nina: keep customer updated at 60-minute cadence.
Eli: Draft note suggestion: "We traced the charge to a configuration mismatch during recent canary deployments which caused short warmup instances to be billed. We will credit 38 reserved GPU-hours to your account and apply a one-day dedicated-capacity goodwill credit while we deploy a fix."
Sam: CSV uploaded: https://redwood.internal/drive/recon/rp-acme-platform-01-recon-20261215.csv (columns: ts,event,instance,billed_gpu_hours,tokens_served).
Nina: customer wants ETA — I'll tell them first update in ~1h. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Zane: I'll also add a metric alert so we catch pools where billed_hours > (token_baseline_hours + 10%) in real time.
Maya: good call. Let's follow up after the hotfix roll.
Eli: will prepare support ticket with reconciled numbers and proposed credits.
Nina: resolved for now — keeping thread open until credits applied and hotfix deployed.
